scan-to-pdf.formula:
scale = min((A4W − 2×margin) / imgWpt, (A4H − 2×margin) / imgHpt, 1)
imgWpt = pixels × 72 / 96

Example: a 4032×3024 px photo → 3024 × 2268 pt.
scale = min(523.28/3024, 769.89/2268) = min(0.173, 0.339) = 0.173.

howTo: Choose camera mode and allow camera access when asked.
Point at the document and tap capture for each page.
Or switch to upload mode and pick existing photos.
Reorder thumbnails with the move buttons; remove mistakes.
Click create to build the PDF and download it.
keyFacts: Camera mode uses getUserMedia to stream your device camera and capture full-resolution frames.
Upload mode accepts PNG and JPG images up to 15 MB each as an alternative to the camera.
Captured pages can be reordered and removed before the PDF is built.
Each image is centered on an A4 page with 36 pt margins, scaled to fit without distortion.
The PDF is assembled locally with pdf-lib; nothing is ever uploaded.

scan-to-pdf.workedExample:
You scan 3 receipt photos at 4032×3024 px.
Each converts to 3024 × 2268 pt (×72/96).
Fit scale: min(523.28/3024, 769.89/2268) = 0.173.
Each page: image 523.3 × 392.4 pt centered on A4 (x=36, y=224.7).
Result: scanned-document.pdf with 3 crisp A4 pages, a few hundred KB each.
